record: independent adversarial review of the prepared paired static-vs-band test (Workflow run wf_50aa30aa-458, four read-only reviewers, 2026-09-22)
note: Verbatim reviewer outputs. Reviewer agreement is not evidence by itself (CLAUDE.md 7.1); WITHDRAWN.json records which findings were independently verified and how.

reviews.summary:
Scope: the future evidence driver (pairing_driver.py), its tests, and the parts of the workflow that affect evidence. Snapshot: the reviewed files are now committed at HEAD 72aec54, byte-identical to what I reviewed (pairing_driver.py sha256 2ef47711…, predeclaration.json 3f588d2e…). I changed nothing in the repository; git status, including ignored files, was the same before and after. I solved no system on the QMHP mesh. My only work on that mesh was read-only counting: 64,434 tets, 1,880 marked by the box, conductors of 9,244 and 189 nodes.

How I checked the driver: I ran a local Palace build of the pinned tree on synthetic geometries only. It is v0.13.0 at a61c8cbe with the first-moment patch, which does not touch geodata.cpp, where Palace loads, refines and saves the mesh. The geometries were a structured slab and an unstructured two-dielectric gmsh box. Each had level-1 and level-2 box runs made exactly as the driver makes them. I then passed the real Palace outputs through pd.execute with only the Palace call replaced (it copies Palace's actual output files instead of launching Palace).

Result: the attempt as prepared cannot reach a verdict. There are three independent blockers:
(1) the MFEM reader refuses the mesh Palace actually saves, so the attempt FAILS at level 1 after two Palace solves;
(2) even with the reader fixed, the nesting check marks Palace's genuinely nested level-1→2 step as not nested, so the result is UNQUALIFIED;
(3) the integrity check requires exactly 6 modes, but Palace writes every converged mode, and more than 6 occurred in both committed rungs that used a 2-level box.
The driver's tests pass (I ran them read-only: 7 passed) because the fake Palace in the tests writes the driver's own mesh format, refines by red refinement, and always returns 6 modes. None of that is what Palace does.

What I checked that holds:
- The _run_palace call matches its signature. The container runs in /work with config.json, the Mesh key is relative and Output is "postpro".
- Palace saves the refined mesh at <Output>/<mesh stem>.mesh, so postpro/coupled_chip_cell_L2.mesh is the right path. MGMaxLevels 1 does make pinned Palace save it; I confirmed this on synthetic runs.
- Palace's DimensionalizeMesh puts coordinates back in mesh units: the level-0 to level-1 vertex offset was exactly 0.
- band() reads the correct columns of the real eig.csv and port-EPR.csv (Re f is column 1, backward error column 4, p[1] column 1). I compared against committed files.
- The box marks 1,880 base tets, as the report says.
- The static model matches the Palace config: PEC attributes 2 and 4, port attribute 10 in +Y, the same L and the same ε.
- Palace adds boundary elements at material interfaces with new attributes above the existing ones. They do not disturb the static solve: on Palace-saved synthetic meshes the port voltage is ±1, the gradient on PEC edges is 0, and the energy identities hold to ≤3.5e-15.
- The manifest is written and verified on success and on any exception inside the try block, and the record directory is created immediately before that try. GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=="1" is enforced.
- A timeout, a DOF refusal or a non-zero return code gives FAILED with palace_run.json kept.
- Extrapolating the DOF count linearly from the N1R/N2R growth (221 marked tets, +4,541 ND unknowns, level-2/level-1 added ratio 4.17) gives about 118.6k at level 1 and 279.6k at level 2. Both are inside the report's estimate and under the 450k cap.

Scratch evidence is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-QMHP-CEM/7e301b81-9cc3-5878-8c8a-f1390dcdb988/scratchpad/redteam/driver/: synth/, uns/, rc/ (runs with RemoveCurvature), e2e.py, e2e2.py, nest_synth.py, refines.py, bary.py and integ.py.

findings.title: read_mfem_mesh refuses the mesh Palace actually saves (a nodes section), so the attempt FAILS at level 1 after two Palace solves
findings.evidence:
Pinned Palace always gives the mesh a nodes grid function. LoadMesh calls mesh->EnsureNodes() unless Model.RemoveCurvature is set (geodata.cpp:1554-1570), and the base config does not set it. The committed logs agree: L2, N1R and N2R all print 'Mesh curvature order: 1'.

On saving, RebalanceMesh takes GetSerialMesh(0) and calls Mesh::Print (geodata.cpp:1403-1438). In MFEM c444b17, GetSerialMesh with Nodes adds every vertex as 0.0 and fills only the nodes (pmesh.cpp ~5466-5500). Mesh::Printer then writes 'vertices N' followed by 'nodes / FiniteElementSpace' and no coordinates (mesh.cpp:11418-11432).

Reproduced with the pinned-tree Palace build on a synthetic slab (Levels 1, SaveAdaptMesh, MGMaxLevels 1). postpro/slab.mesh contains 'vertices
252

nodes
FiniteElementSpace
FiniteElementCollection: H1_3D_P1
VDim: 3
Ordering: 1'. pd.read_mfem_mesh raises ValueError('curved mesh (nodes section): refused').

Replaying the real Palace outputs through pd.execute (e2e.py): Palace was launched for levels [0, 1], then 'EXECUTE RAISED: ValueError curved mesh (nodes section): refused'. failure.json has levels_completed [0], there is no summary.json, and the manifest verifies.
findings.failure_scenario: On the approved run, level 0 and level 1 Palace solves complete, then read_mfem_mesh raises. The record is FAILED, the single attempt is spent, and no verdict is possible.
findings.suggested_fix:
Option 1: parse the H1_3D_P1 nodes section. For P1, dof i is vertex i. Handle Ordering 0 (byNODES) and 1 (byVDIM). Check the collection name, VDim 3 and the count, and refuse anything else.

Option 2: add Model.RemoveCurvature: true to all three configs. I checked this: the saved mesh then has a plain vertices section that the current reader accepts, with identical unknown counts (5529 and 18950 ND unknowns). It changes the config digests, so the predeclaration and approval draft must be regenerated.

Either way, add a test that replays a mesh file written by the pinned Palace.

findings.title: nesting() declares Palace's genuinely nested level-1→2 refinement NOT nested: the 'only coarse-edge midpoints' claim is false for MFEM conforming tet refinement
findings.evidence:
Palace calls GeneralRefinement(refs, -1). For tets this is conforming LocalRefinement: three successive bisections per marked tet, then closure. Within one call it can bisect edges created earlier in the same call.

I ran the pinned Palace on two synthetic geometries, with separate Levels:1 and Levels:2 runs from the base mesh, exactly as the driver does. The level-0 to level-1 step passes in both. The level-1 to level-2 step:
- structured slab: 20 of 634 new vertices are not level-1 edge midpoints (max offset 0.0417 relative). nesting() returns new_vertices_are_coarse_edge_midpoints=false and nested=false.
- unstructured gmsh box: 43 of 2006 new vertices (offset 0.036).

The refinement is genuinely nested. All 4180 of 4180 and 15626 of 15626 level-2 tets lie inside a single level-1 tet, with tet attributes preserved. A barycentric prolongation gives PᵀK₁P = K₀ to 1.56e-15 and 1.69e-15 (bary.py).

The same failure occurs with RemoveCurvature, when the reader is not the problem (rc_nest.py).

Replay through pd.execute with the reader fixed (e2e2.py): integrity_failures includes 'levels 1->2: refinement not verified nested', and the verdict is UNQUALIFIED.
findings.failure_scenario: Even after the reader is fixed, a correct nested refinement is rejected and the one attempt ends UNQUALIFIED. The report's section 4 statement 'every new vertex must be a coarse edge midpoint' and the driver docstring ('bisection and red refinement both add only edge midpoints') misstate what Palace does.
findings.suggested_fix: Build P by point location. Give each fine vertex its barycentric weights in a containing coarse tet, dropping weights below a small tolerance. Require every fine tet to lie inside one coarse tet with its attribute preserved, and the child volumes to sum to the parent's. Then check the Galerkin identity with that P. Keep the existing negative controls, and add a positive control built from real Palace level-1 and level-2 meshes.

findings.title: Integrity requires exactly 6 modes, but Palace writes every converged eigenpair (num_conv > N is common, including both 2-level box rungs)
findings.evidence:
eigensolver.cpp:264-292 postprocesses and writes 'for (int i = 0; i < num_conv; i++)'.

Rows in the committed eig.csv files, all with config N=6:
- L2: 6
- N1R: 6
- L3: 6
- R1: 7
- PO1 (2-level box): 8
- N2R (2-level box): 9

My synthetic level-0 run with N=2 wrote 6 rows ('Found 6 converged eigenvalues').

predeclaration.integrity.modes_saved = 6, and integrity() flags any n_modes != 6. B_h and H_h are also defined 'over the saved modes'. The report's own figures show the 9-mode N2R band has H/B = 0.9912 against 0.996 for the 6-mode bands. That 0.5% shift is half the 1% SUPPORTS drift window.
findings.failure_scenario: Level 2 (a 2-level box, like N2R and PO1) returns 7-9 modes, so the run is UNQUALIFIED and the attempt is spent. If the check were simply loosened to ≥ 6, B would be averaged over different numbers of modes at different levels. That could create drift of the size the table uses to decide SUPPORTS versus CONTRADICTS.
findings.suggested_fix: Pre-declare the band as the lowest 6 modes by Re f at every level, and require num_conv ≥ 6. Keep all rows in the raw evidence. Regenerate the predeclaration and approval draft.

findings.title: The tests certify a fake Palace that does not behave like Palace, and include a test that locks in blocker 1
findings.evidence:
The fake Palace in _synthetic_world:
- writes its meshes with pd.write_mfem_mesh (a vertices section, no nodes);
- builds levels 1 and 2 with af.refine_red, which adds only midpoints;
- always writes exactly 6 eig.csv rows.

test_the_mfem_reader_refuses_what_it_cannot_read asserts that a nodes section is refused, which is exactly the format Palace writes. I ran the 7 driver tests read-only (end_to_end, failure_mid, refuses_what, round_trip) and all passed, while the same driver fails on real Palace output (e2e.py).

No test makes integrity() fail: nothing covers the DOF cap, a missing DOF, the mode count, backward error, N_B > 1, nesting not verified, C rising, or level-0 reproduction. No test covers execute() with timed_out, returncode != 0 or a DOF refusal.

The report's section 5 says 'The end-to-end synthetic tests prove both paths with a mock Palace'.
findings.failure_scenario: CI stays green and the approval is requested on the strength of tests that cannot detect blockers 1-3. That misstates what is proved.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit a small fixture produced by the pinned Palace on a synthetic mesh: SaveAdaptMesh output with a nodes section, a 2-level box, and eig.csv with num_conv > N. Replay it through execute(). Add negative-control tests for each integrity() rule, and for the timeout, non-zero return code and DOF-refusal paths. Correct section 5 of the report.

findings.title: The evidence commit pushes without rebasing: if the branch moves during the run, the record is never committed
findings.evidence: The commit step runs 'git push origin "HEAD:$BRANCH"' with no pull. The ladder workflow does 'git pull --rebase --autostash origin ...' before pushing (palace-order1-ladder.yml:232-233). This branch is actively being committed to: 72aec54 says review fixes 'will follow in a separate commit'.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone pushes to the branch during the roughly 30-60 minute run, so the push is rejected as non-fast-forward. The record then exists only in a 90-day artifact. The driver's one-attempt check (a glob over committed results/) cannot see it, which leaves the run-number binding as the only guard (see the next finding).
findings.suggested_fix: Rebase before pushing, with a bounded retry, as the ladder does. Or push to a dedicated evidence branch. Fail loudly if the record is not in the pushed tree.

findings.title: The one-attempt binding is to environment variables anyone can set, not to the workflow's identity
findings.evidence:
require_approval checks only str(GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER) == str(approval.github_run_number) and GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT == '1'. It does not check GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF or GITHUB_REPOSITORY. Whatever workflow first runs this driver has run number 1, and so does a local shell exporting both variables.

An approval with no github_run_number key passes whenever GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER is also unset, because 'None' == 'None'.
findings.failure_scenario: The approval is committed, and the CI record is still in flight or was not pushed (previous finding). A local or other-workflow run with GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER=1 and GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=1 then passes the gate and runs a second attempt.
findings.suggested_fix: Require an integer github_run_number in the approval. Require GITHUB_ACTIONS=='true', GITHUB_REPOSITORY equal to the expected repository, and GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF to start with '<repo>/.github/workflows/static-band-pairing.yml@'.

findings.title: Scratch-directory checks happen only after the attempt is spent
findings.evidence:
rec.mkdir(exist_ok=False) runs first. Only afterwards, inside the loop, does work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False) run. An existing scratch/level0 therefore raises FileExistsError, which is recorded as FAILED with zero solves.

scratch is also never resolved to an absolute path. _run_palace passes f'{solver_dir}:/work' to docker -v, and docker does not treat a bare relative path as a host directory.
findings.failure_scenario: A rerun in the same job, or a local invocation with an existing or relative --scratch, spends the attempt without launching Palace.
findings.suggested_fix: Before rec.mkdir, resolve scratch to an absolute path, and refuse if any level directory already exists or if the image or runtime is unavailable.

findings.title: nesting() pairs coarse and fine conductors by size rank, which local refinement can reverse
findings.evidence:
conductor_components sorts components largest first. The check compares fine component k with coarse component k.

On the synthetic slab refined by Palace:
- level 1: [28 nodes (ground, attr 2), 18 (island, attr 4)]
- level 2: [52 nodes (island, attr 4), 28 (ground, attr 2)]

The static solve's port voltage flipped to -1.0 at level 2, which confirms the swap. For QMHP (9,244 against 189 nodes at level 0) a swap within 2 levels is unlikely, so this is latent.
findings.failure_scenario: If box refinement grows the island's node count past the ground's, a correct refinement is reported as having non-nested constraint sets, and the result is UNQUALIFIED.
findings.suggested_fix: Match components through coarse-vertex membership, or through their PEC attribute, instead of size order.

findings.title: integrity() does not require complete nesting evidence or real refinement, and an unrefined run would read as LOW POWER
findings.evidence:
integ.py: integrity() returns [] when there is only one nesting record, or none. It never checks that n_tets increases from level to level.

RebalanceMesh, and with it the mesh save, is called whenever max_region_ref_levels > 0, even if no element is marked (geodata.cpp:353-356). A box that marks nothing therefore produces three identical meshes, g = 1, and the verdict 'UNRESOLVED: LOW POWER … the static error lies elsewhere'. The current box does mark 1,880 tets, so this is latent.
findings.failure_scenario: A config or unit error that leaves the mesh unrefined produces a scientific interpretation (the error lies outside the box) instead of UNQUALIFIED.
findings.suggested_fix: Require len(nest) == len(levels) - 1 with consecutive from/to values, strictly increasing n_tets, new_vertices > 0, and a level-1 marked count consistent with the predeclared 1,880.

findings.title: Evidence-preservation gaps on the edge paths
findings.evidence:
(a) PALACE_OUTPUTS leaves out surface-Q.csv. The base config's Postprocessing.Dielectric produces it (it is in the committed L2 postpro), so it never reaches the committed record.
(b) The refined meshes are the inputs to the decisive S_1 and S_2 but are kept only as a 90-day artifact.
(c) _run_palace writes palace_log.txt only after wait() returns, so a KeyboardInterrupt or cancellation during a solve loses that level's whole log.
(d) If _finish raises on the success path, the except branch writes failure.json next to a summary.json that carries a verdict, giving a contradictory record.
(e) SIGKILL or an OOM kill leaves no failure.json and no manifest. The commit step's condition does not require the manifest step to have succeeded, so a record without a manifest would be committed.
findings.failure_scenario: Raw output or decisive inputs become unrecoverable after 90 days, or the preserved record contradicts itself or has no manifest.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy every file in postpro except the .mesh, or list surface-Q.csv explicitly. Attach the refined meshes to an immutable release, or record that regeneration is deterministic and bind it by hash. Stream the log to the scratch directory during the run. On the success path, keep a _finish failure separate from failure.json. In the workflow, if the manifest is missing, write a clearly labelled external failure note plus a manifest before committing, or refuse the commit.

findings.title: The power rule masks a large δ (sheet-port departure) as LOW POWER
findings.evidence: decide() checks g < 1.05 first, so max|δ| > 0.03 with g < 1.05 is returned as 'UNRESOLVED: LOW POWER'. δ can be measured at a single level and does not depend on the static quantity moving.
findings.failure_scenario: A departure of the port from the lumped element large enough to count as CONTRADICTS is reported only as low power.
findings.suggested_fix: Point this out to the approver explicitly, or evaluate δ > 0.03 before the power condition in a new predeclaration.

findings.title: The 450k DOF cap raises the standing 250k rule without saying so
findings.evidence: The ladder states a 250,000-DOF rule that 'This script may not raise either' (palace_order1_ladder.py:91,115-116). The pairing sets dof_cap_per_level to 450,000, and neither the report nor the approval draft mentions the 250k rule. My extrapolation from N1R/N2R puts level 2 at about 279.6k, above 250k, so the increase is actually needed.
findings.failure_scenario: The approver grants a compute-budget increase without seeing that it is one (CLAUDE.md section 3).
findings.suggested_fix: State the increase over the 250k rule in the report and the approval draft, so that it is approved explicitly.

reviews.summary:
Adversarial review of the maths and the two verification claims in docs/coupled-candidate/static-band-pairing.md and experiments/static-band-pairing/. The review target was the uncommitted working tree on HEAD ebcf5e2. I modified nothing under /home/user/QMHP-CEM: the __pycache__ timestamps predate my runs, and later runs used -B. I ran no solve and no eigen-solve on the QMHP mesh (reads and assembly only). All solves were on synthetic geometry in scratch/redteam/math/.

CLAIMS THAT HOLD (checked independently):
(a1) The continuum upper bound C <= C_h holds for any H1-conforming mesh. The 543 'extension' edges only force the P1 function to 1 on extra edges, which can only raise C_h, so the bound survives. static_capacitance.py computes the energy as the quadratic form of an exactly constrained vector (lines 95-102).
(a2) Monotonicity is certified algebraically by the Galerkin identity plus constraint inclusion. From P^T K1 P = K0, and P mapping the coarse admissible set into the fine one, it follows that C_{h+1} <= a1(Pu*,Pu*) = C_h. Geometric nesting is not needed for that step. I reproduced galerkin_identity_rel = 6.917e-15 and 543 extension edges on the L2 mesh (assembly only).
(a3) The continuum problem is well posed: Lipschitz sheets have positive capacity and island and ground are disjoint. The mesh is a solid box: read-only check shows all 3040 multiplicity-1 faces lie on the bounding-box planes and are tagged attr 2, and there are 2 conductor components. The relative cohomology is therefore H^1(M,A) = R^{2-1}, so there are no extra harmonic fields in the curl-curl null space.
(b1) I re-derived the lumped identities: N=1; sum p/lambda = L C_h/V^2 (the solution of Kx=f is x = L grad(phi*)); Parseval sum p lambda = f^T M^-1 f/L; S <= B_k/N_k by Cauchy-Schwarz (valid for any subset of modes).
(b2) spectral.py checks out:
- curl(lam_a grad lam_b - lam_b grad lam_a) = 2 grad lam_a x grad lam_b;
- the lo->hi sign convention and local edge table are identical to anchor_fem.whitney_mass;
- the 2-D trace Whitney mass has the correct sign pattern and area(1+d_ij)/12;
- L_s = L (w/l) n_elem matches GetToSquare (lumpedportoperator.hpp:57-60, used at lumpedportoperator.cpp:585);
- the voltage functional coefficient 1/(w n) matches lumpedportoperator.cpp:212;
- p = 1/2 L |I|^2/E_elec with I = V/(i omega L) (postoperator.cpp:644-659, eigensolver.cpp:347) equals spectral.py's (f.E)^2/(L lambda E^T M E);
- w and l come from the bounding box (lumpedelement.cpp).
(b3) The |p| convention is correct: Palace's sign is sign(Re I) only.
(b4) The L2 port face is an exact rectangle: 25 triangles, area/(l*w) = 1.0000000000000002, ground nodes only at y=-0.115 and island nodes only at y=-0.075. So V(grad phi) = 1.
(b5) Measured values reproduce: L2 delta_band = 6.585e-4 and S0/B0 = 0.99672.
The report's two-node formula is correct as algebra (with conditions; see findings).

MAIN DEFECT: the report and pre-declaration miss an exact identity for Palace's own sheet-port pencil. For it, N = 1 and sum over all modes of p/lambda = L C'_h. Here C'_h is the static Dirichlet capacitance with the port-face potential held linear along l-hat. So delta_h = C'_h/C_h - 1 >= 0 exactly, and it can be computed by one static solve.
- Verified with no fitting: the static formula reproduces identities.json's dense-eigen delta to 1e-12 (n=3: 0.022957366735 vs 0.022957366734; n=4: 0.029935602107 vs 0.029935602108).
- On an internal coplanar island-gap-port geometry it gives 0.019714615582 vs dense-eigen 0.019714615576, with N-1 = -2.7e-12.
- It does not depend on K_curl: 3.7*Kc and a curl-curl with random per-tet weights give identical N and delta.
Consequence: on every mesh, S_h equals (1+delta_h) times Palace's complete harmonic moment. 'Co-movement' is therefore a theorem, not an untested prediction. The planned test's delta is a static quantity measured through Palace, and SUPPORTS is essentially forced whenever g >= 1.05. This is the same non-independence the report itself identifies for r0 in its correction 1.

SECOND DEFECT (outside the maths lens but concrete, read-only): the refinement box does not contain the ground edge on two of the four sides. The gap is 0.040 mm on the x-, y- and y+ sides and 0.020 mm only on x+. Only 9 of 234 tets touching the x- ground edge are marked, and 22 of 221 on the y+ edge.

Smaller issues: the conformity check misses hanging nodes, and the driver runs no conformity check at all; delta depends on mesh resolution and the 3% window was calibrated on a coarse mesh; the CONTRADICTS reason string always says 'decouple'; the report says A diverges only for the sheet port; the two-node reduction's conditions are unstated; the verification tests cannot detect an error in the curl-curl operator; the two energy routes are called independent when they share inputs.

The UNRESOLVED verdict and Route A are not affected by any of this.

findings.title: Palace's sheet-port pencil has an exact static identity (N=1, sum p/lambda = L C'_h), so 'co-movement' is a theorem and delta is derived, not measured; the paired test's SUPPORTS is essentially predetermined
findings.evidence:
DERIVATION. Let psi be 0 on ground, 1 on the island, and linear along l-hat on the rectangular port face. Then Kc grad(psi) = 0, and Ks grad(psi) = (1/L_s)(1/l) int l-hat.y dS = f.y/L exactly when L_s = L w/l. So x = L grad(psi*) solves Kx = f, where psi* is the energy minimiser under those Dirichlet data. Null(K) is {grad chi : chi = 0 on the conductors and on the port face}. Hence:
- N = f^T x/L = V(psi*) = 1;
- sum_all p/lambda = x^T M x/L = L C'_h;
- delta_h = C'_h/C_h - 1 >= 0.

NUMERICAL CHECKS (static constrained solve only, scratch/redteam/math/delta_static.py and coplanar_dense2.py):
- Slab n=3: delta_static = 0.022957366735481655 vs identities.json sheet 0.022957366734422502.
- Slab n=4: 0.02993560210718238 vs 0.02993560210839763.
- Internal coplanar port (the QMHP topology): static 0.01971461558180 vs dense-eigen 0.01971461557601, with N-1 = -2.7e-12.
- kc_insensitive.py: replacing Kc with 3.7*Kc, or with a random-weight curl-curl that has the same kernel, leaves N and delta unchanged to 1e-11.

WHERE THE DOCUMENTS CONTRADICT THIS:
- The report calls delta 'measured' (lines 99-116; section 3 table, line 151).
- It lists 'band and static co-move under refinement' as 'prediction, untested' (line 153).
- pairing_driver.py:18 calls delta 'a measured perturbation'.
- predeclaration.json:7 and :9 frame co-movement as a prediction.
- Yet predeclaration.json:112 itself admits 'r_h [can] change only through the band's dispersion (H/B) and delta'.

TRUNCATION IS NEGLIGIBLE. With N=1, the out-of-band part is at most S_h(1-N_B)/f_max^2, which is about 1.8e-5 relative on L2. So decide()'s delta = S_h/H_h - 1 is the static C'_h/C_h - 1 to within 2e-5.
findings.failure_scenario: The single approved attempt runs. g = 1.2 (box refinement moves S). delta_h comes out at about 7e-4, 1.3e-3 and 2e-3. This follows from statics: in the coplanar synthetic, delta grows about 3x over two nested levels. H/B stays near 0.996, so the drift is about 0.2%, and the verdict is SUPPORTS: 'the band moves with the static quantity, as the identity predicts'. That result would be reported as support for co-movement. In fact it was fixed by a theorem once g >= 1.05, and delta could have been computed without Palace. Three consequential Palace solves would be spent confirming an identity, and the evidential weight of SUPPORTS would be misstated, exactly as the report says of r0 in its correction 1.
findings.suggested_fix:
1. State the Palace-pencil theorem in section 2/3 with its conditions: a rectangular port whose conductor nodes lie only on its two end lines (true on L2: area/(l*w) = 1.0000000000000002; ground nodes only at y=-0.115, island nodes only at y=-0.075).
2. Relabel delta as derived. Add C'_h (the port-face-linear constrained static solve) to the static computation at every level.
3. Reframe what the Palace runs can establish. They add only two things:
   - an implementation-consistency check, |S_h*sum_B|p|/f^2 - C'_h/C_h| <= S_h(1-N_B)/f_max^2;
   - the B_h/H_h dispersion drift.
4. Remove 'co-movement' as the tested hypothesis, or explicitly state that SUPPORTS is not independent evidence. Decide under human approval whether the test is still worth its one attempt.

findings.title: Refinement box omits the ground edge on the x- and y+ sides; the stated rationale ('the whole 0.020 mm gap') is false, because the gap is 0.040 mm on three sides
findings.evidence:
Read-only inspection of the committed L2 mesh (no solve).

Ground-plane cutout edges in the z=0 plane:
- x- side: x = -0.715 (gap 0.040);
- x+ side: x = -0.505 (gap 0.020);
- y- side: y = -0.115 (gap 0.040);
- y+ side: y = +0.115 (gap 0.040).

The box is x in [-0.7,-0.5], y in [-0.125,0.1].

Tets touching each singular edge, and how many have a vertex in the box (Palace's marking rule, geodata.cpp):

| edge | touching | marked |
|---|---|---|
| x- ground | 234 | 9 |
| y+ ground | 221 | 22 |
| y- ground | 212 | 194 |
| x+ ground | 142 | 142 |
| island | 1022 | 1022 |

Marked base tets = 1880, which matches the report.

The false statements are in predeclaration.json:32 and report lines 164-167: 'covers ... the whole 0.020 mm gap to ground' and 'about two elements'.
findings.failure_scenario: Two of the four ground-edge field singularities facing the island stay at level-0 resolution, apart from closure. Static growth g is reduced, and the region carrying part of the static error is excluded. If g < 1.05, the frozen LOW POWER reading ('the static error then lies outside the box') would be recorded. The cause would actually be that the box was drawn from a wrong gap width. The single attempt would be spent with needlessly reduced power.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the rationale and the gap widths. Either widen the box to include the ground edges (x >= -0.725, y <= 0.125) and re-derive the marked-tet count, the DOF estimate and the config sha256s, or keep the box and state explicitly that the x- and y+ ground edges are excluded. Qualify the LOW POWER interpretation accordingly. This needs re-review before approval.

findings.title: The conformity criterion ('<=2 tets per face', tagged triangles are faces, no coincident nodes) and the Galerkin identity both accept a hanging-node mesh; the driver checks no conformity for Palace meshes, yet calls S_continuum >= S_2 rigorous
findings.evidence:
hanging2.py: _slab(4), with 72 of 768 interior tets red-refined without closure.
- vn.conformity returns {max_face_multiplicity: 2, every_tagged_triangle_is_a_tet_face: True, coincident_nodes: 0}.
- Only boundary_faces changes, 320 -> 1400, and nothing checks it.
- pairing_driver.nesting returns nested = True, galerkin_identity_rel = 3.6e-16, constraint_sets_nested = True.

The Galerkin identity certifies monotonicity only. The upper bound C <= C_h needs H1-conformity.

The report's row 'outer boundary: all 3,040 faces are grounded walls' (line 37) is TRUE: I checked that all 3040 multiplicity-1 faces lie on the bbox planes and carry attr 2. But neither verify_nesting.py nor nesting_verification.json produces or records it, although the report cites that file for it. pairing_driver.nesting (lines 193-239) runs no conformity check, while predeclaration.json:79 lists 'the rigorous one-sided bound S_continuum >= S_2 ... (nesting verified)'.
findings.failure_scenario: A nonconforming refined mesh, or any mesh whose multiplicity-1 faces are not all on the outer boundary, passes as 'conforming and nested'. Its C_h can then lie below the continuum C, and a non-bound is reported as a 'rigorous one-sided bound'. In practice MFEM conforming bisection plus read_mfem_mesh's refusal of NC sections make this unlikely, so the gap is in the verification logic, not in the current meshes.
findings.suggested_fix: In conformity() and in the driver, require every multiplicity-1 face to lie on the declared outer boundary (the bbox planes) and to be tagged. Record this in the JSON. Do not call the level-2 bound rigorous unless this check passes on the Palace-saved mesh.

findings.title: delta depends on mesh resolution (in coplanar gap geometries it grows under refinement), the 3% CONTRADICTS window was calibrated on one coarse mesh, and decide() labels a delta-triggered CONTRADICTS as 'decouple'
findings.evidence:
Static-only nested red refinement, delta = C'/C - 1:
- Slab _slab(4): 2.99% -> 2.04% -> 1.66%.
- Coplanar island/gap/port synthetic, about 2 elements across the gap at level 0: 0.40% -> 0.90% -> 1.34% (port width 1/8 of the island perimeter) and 0.96% -> 2.19% -> 3.21% (port = island width), while C drops 14% and then 7%.
- Second coplanar geometry: 1.97% -> 4.63% -> 6.84%.

predeclaration.json:112 justifies 3% as 'the sheet-vs-lumped perturbation of a synthetic port face comparable to the whole structure'. That number is the coarse n=4 slab value, and it falls to 1.7% under refinement of the same slab.

pairing_driver.py:286 always gives the reason 'the band and the static quantity decouple under refinement', even when the only trigger is max|delta| > 0.03.
findings.failure_scenario: Palace's sheet-port effect is under-resolved on coarse gap meshes. Resolving it raises delta, so the SUPPORTS reading 'sheet port within 1% of the lumped element' depends on the mesh rather than the device. For the QMHP port (delta_0 = 6.6e-4, port about 3% of the island perimeter) a ~3x growth gives about 2e-3, so the verdict is probably unchanged. However, any CONTRADICTS caused by delta would be written into summary.json as 'decouple', which misstates the cause.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute delta_h statically (C'_h) and report its refinement trend. Justify the windows on resolved values, not a single coarse synthetic. Make decide() report which condition triggered: 'decouple (drift)' vs 'sheet port departs (delta)'.

findings.title: 'The complete first moment A ... diverges for the sheet port': A is the same for both port models
findings.evidence: Line 86. A = sum_all p lambda = f^T M^-1 f / L (Parseval), which does not involve K. identities.py uses the same A_direct for the lumped and sheet checks, and both agree to 1e-16. The divergence under refinement comes from f being a surface functional (not L2-bounded), so it holds for the lumped port too. static_capacitance.synthetic_controls already shows it growing.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader infers that the lumped model has a finite complete first moment. Any argument that relies on that (for example, using A as a lumped reference) would be wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that A diverges under refinement for both port models, because it depends only on f and M.

findings.title: The two-node relation B/S = C_FF (C^-1)_FF = 1/(1-k^2) needs unstated conditions, and the QMHP mesh has no second conductor
findings.evidence:
Lines 118-126; predeclaration.json:8.

Derivation: for K = diag(1/L_F, 1/L_2) and M = C, sum p/lambda = L_F C_FF and sum p lambda = (C^-1)_FF/L_F. So B/S = C_FF (C^-1)_FF only if:
(i) node 2 is DC-grounded through its own inductance;
(ii) every mode of the reduction is in the band.

If node 2 is DC-floating, the static C is 1/(C^-1)_FF and B/S = 1.

The mesh has exactly two conductor components (9244 and 189 nodes: ground and island). So 'C_FF' and '(C^-1)_FF' are not quantities of the meshed problem; k_eff is only a name for 1 - H/B.
findings.failure_scenario: The identifications 'H corresponds to 1/(C_FF L_F)' and 'B corresponds to (C^-1)_FF/L_F' (the registered E_C) are read as derived from the mesh. They are then used to interpret the band dispersion as a Schur gap, which the static solve on a two-conductor mesh cannot represent.
findings.suggested_fix: State conditions (i) and (ii). State that the mesh supplies no second conductor. Present 1 - k^2_eff = H/B as a definition, not a derived circuit quantity.

findings.title: With N=1 provable for Palace's pencil, the L2 delta has a two-sided bound; this also resolves the open item in fem-spectral-mapping section 3, and a zero-Palace cross-check exists
findings.evidence: L2: 1-N_B = 6.26e-4. All out-of-band modes are above f_6 = 8.7069 GHz, since shift-invert returns the 6 modes closest to the 0.5 GHz target. So sum_out p/f^2 <= 6.26e-4/75.81 = 8.3e-6, which gives delta_L2 in [6.585e-4, 6.76e-4]. The report gives only 'delta >= 6.6e-4', and its correction 2 ('unreachable by a wide margin for Palace's pencil') needs the upper bound. fem-spectral-mapping.md section 3 retained '1 - N >= 0 as an unmeasured quantity' and asked whether 'the DC tangential profile ... is exactly uniform'. It is: K u = q forces grad_t(phi) = (L/l) l-hat on the port. identities.json sheet N = 1 to 1e-12 (n=3,4) is not mentioned in the report.
findings.failure_scenario: The report attributes delta = 6.6e-4 to 'the sheet port's effect'. That attribution is an assumption: a mismatch between Palace's and the static discrete problems at the 1e-3 level would look the same. The static prediction C'_0/C_0 - 1 in [6.585e-4, 6.76e-4] would test the whole chain against the already-executed L2 Palace run with no new Palace solve.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the two-sided bound and the N=1 theorem with its conditions. Offer the C'_0 static solve on the L2 mesh as a cross-check. It is a solve on the QMHP mesh, so it needs human approval under this project's rules.

findings.title: The known-answer identity checks cannot detect an error in the curl-curl operator (only its kernel matters)
findings.evidence:
kc_insensitive.py, slab n=3. With Kc, 3.7*Kc, or a curl-curl with random per-tet weights in [0.1,10]:
- lumped N-1 is at most 6e-12 and delta at most 1.3e-11;
- sheet delta = 0.0229573667 in every case.
Only the truncated quantity min_k (B_k/N_k)/S changes (0.9791 vs 0.9785). curl_grad_rel checks the kernel only.
findings.failure_scenario: 'Verified to machine precision' is read as validating spectral.curl_curl. A scaling or assembly error in K_curl would pass every identity check while changing the truncated statement 'S <= B_k/N_k can fail by up to 2.7%'.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the identities are independent of K_curl beyond its null space. If the truncated moments matter, add a known-answer test of K_curl itself (for example, analytic cavity eigenvalues on a box mesh).

findings.title: 'Two independent energy evaluations' share phi, the mesh and epsilon; they are an identity check, not independent confirmation
findings.evidence: Line 64. static_capacitance.py:106-111 evaluates (G phi)^T M (G phi) with the same phi, mesh and eps_r as phi^T K phi. Their agreement verifies the discrete de Rham identity G^T M G = K_P1. It does not independently confirm C. CLAUDE.md section 7 forbids treating shared-input agreement as independent confirmation.
findings.failure_scenario: The 82.2 fF bound is presented as independently confirmed when both evaluations would share any error in the mesh, epsilon, constraint sets or length scale.
findings.suggested_fix: Call it an assembly-consistency identity, not an independent evaluation.

reviews.summary:
Palace/MFEM source lens, reviewed against frozen snapshot HEAD 72aec54. The work under review is now committed there, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. Pinned sources: Palace v0.13.0 a61c8cbe at /home/user/awslabs/palace; MFEM c444b17c (cmake/ExternalGitTags.cmake:135) with Palace's 7 extern/patch/mfem patches applied, cloned and built serial in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-QMHP-CEM/7e301b81-9cc3-5878-8c8a-f1390dcdb988/scratchpad/redteam/palace-lens/.

Method. A scratch emulator (emulate.cpp) replays Palace's single-rank mesh path using Palace's own code for CheckMesh, the box-marking loop and the save:
- LoadMesh, then EnsureNodes, then CheckMesh(clean, add_bdr);
- a reload with Finalize(refine=1, fix=1), as ParMesh::Load does;
- nondimensionalisation, the box loop, then GeneralRefinement(refs, -1);
- dimensionalisation, then Mesh::Print.

It reproduces the committed Palace logs exactly: 9,449 interface triangles added; N1R 68,299 elements / 14,667 vertices / 84,485 edges / 138,118 faces; N2R 84,445 / 17,447 / 103,411 / 170,410. On the QMHP mesh I ran only mesh refinement and geometry/assembly checks. No linear system or eigenproblem was solved on it or on any refinement, and nothing under /home/user/QMHP-CEM was written.

Three blocking defects each independently turn the one approved attempt into FAILED or UNQUALIFIED for reasons unrelated to the physics:
- **B1:** the saved mesh has a `nodes` section, which the driver refuses.
- **B2:** the driver's nesting predicate rejects Palace's nested second-level bisection refinement.
- **B3:** Palace writes every converged mode, but integrity requires exactly 6.

Checked and holds:
1. Saving the mesh.
   - With box levels greater than 0 and a single-mesh vector (MGMaxLevels 1: no mesh.reserve; the N1R/N2R logs have no Coarse/Refined lines, while N2 has them), RefineMesh calls RebalanceMesh (geodata.cpp:352-355).
   - RebalanceMesh writes `<Problem.Output>/<stem of Model.Mesh>.mesh` = postpro/coupled_chip_cell_L2.mesh (geodata.cpp:1403-1412). The driver's SAVED_MESH_NAME and path are correct.
   - It is written once: after all box levels, before rebalancing (none at np=1), before the solve, and never at level 0.
   - postpro/ already exists: the BaseSolver constructor creates it (basesolver.cpp:115-117) before ReadMesh (main.cpp:311).
   - Units are mm (GetLengthScale = Lc/L0, iodata.hpp:49; L = 4 exactly). Print uses scientific notation with max_digits10 digits, so coarse vertices round-trip with 0 offset.
   - The header is "MFEM mesh v1.0" with no mfem_mesh_end. Saving has no side effect on the solved ParMesh, because it prints a serial copy.
2. Box marking.
   - An element is marked if any vertex lies inside the box, inclusive (geodata.cpp:231-298). On the Nodes path this uses GlobGeometryRefiner, whose default type is ClosedUniform (geom.hpp:338), so the points are the vertices. Nothing else in Palace uses the refiner.
   - 1,880 marked tets reproduced. No vertex lies exactly on a box face.
   - One level is LocalRefinement type 3: 7 bisections into 8, then green closure (mesh.cpp:10509-10560, 9896+). ParMesh at np=1 runs the same loop, because the group exchange is skipped (pmesh.cpp:3355+).
3. Boundary elements.
   - Internal PEC (4), port (10), interface (25) and 11/12 triangles are bisected by BdrBisection with their attributes kept.
   - On the emulated levels 1 and 2, per-attribute areas are conserved exactly (2: 62.88, 4: 15.54632, 10: 0.0008 mm²), every triangle is a tet face, volume stays 30.88, and there are exactly two conductors (L1 [9431, 660], L2 [10278, 2451]).
   - The 0→1 step passes the driver's own nesting check (3,309/3,309 midpoints; Galerkin 1.7e-15).
4. Mesh loading.
   - ReadMesh(reorder=false, clean_elem=true, add_bdr=true) removes no tets and adds 9,449 attribute-25 interface triangles (log and emulation). Attributes 11 and 12 are kept.
   - ReorientTetMesh is off by default; fix_orientation and marking only permute local vertex order.
   - static_capacitance ignores attributes other than PEC and port, so the saved-mesh geometry equals Palace's discrete mesh and conductor detection by attributes 2 and 4 is correct.
5. Config and CSV outputs.
   - Every key the driver writes is parsed, and no unknown key triggers the parser's `empty()` abort (configfile.cpp:326, 342-372, 1451, 1686).
   - Save gates only PostprocessFields (eigensolver.cpp:351). MGMaxLevels changes only the mesh-vector capacity and the preconditioner hierarchy, not the discrete eigenproblem.
   - eig.csv columns are (m, Re f, Im f, Q, Bkwd, Abs) and port-EPR.csv is (m, p[1]); the driver's indices match (eigensolver.cpp:436-455).
   - p = copysign(½L|I|²/E_m, Re I), with I = V/(iωL) and E_m = E_elec + E_cap (postoperator.cpp:644-660). It is rank-one and voltage-based, and its sign is arbitrary, so the driver's abs() is correct.
   - The sheet-port stiffness term 1/Ls is confirmed (lumpedportoperator.cpp:571-590).
6. Feasibility. Emulated DOFs are 102,280 at level 1 and 235,655 at level 2: inside the report's ranges and under the 450k cap. Level 3 is 1,111,691 DOFs, below the stated 1.3–2.9 M, but it is excluded either way.

Not established: the byte-exact Palace output for the pairing box. The emulation is count-validated on N1R/N2R, not on this box.

findings.title: Palace's saved refined mesh carries an order-1 'nodes' section, which read_mfem_mesh refuses, so the attempt dies at level 1 after two Palace solves
findings.evidence:
Source chain:
- The base config has no Model.RemoveCurvature; the default is false (configfile.hpp:209).
- LoadMesh therefore calls mesh->EnsureNodes() (geodata.cpp:1554-1569), which calls SetCurvature(1,...,byVDIM) (MFEM mesh.cpp:6185-6260).
- MeshPartitioner::ExtractPart copies Nodes into the part (mesh.cpp:13827-13840), and MeshPart::Print writes them as 'nodes' (mesh.cpp:13370-13374).
- ParMesh::Load reads them back (pmesh.cpp:960, 981).
- ParMesh::GetSerialMesh gives the serial mesh Nodes and leaves its vertices at 0 (pmesh.cpp:5440-5455).
- Mesh::Printer then prints 'vertices\nNV\n\nnodes\n' plus the FESpace instead of coordinates (mesh.cpp:11358-11377).

Empirical evidence:
- All 52 committed Palace logs, including N1R and N2R (box refinement, MGMaxLevels 1), print 'Mesh curvature order: 1'. That line comes from GetNodes() != nullptr after RefineMesh (geodata.cpp:365-369).
- The count-validated emulation writes 'vertices / 17300 / nodes / FiniteElementSpace / FiniteElementCollection: H1_3D_P1 / VDim: 3 / Ordering: 1'.
- pd.read_mfem_mesh on that file raises ValueError('curved mesh (nodes section): refused') (pairing_driver.py:159-161).

Test coverage:
- tests/test_static_band_pairing.py:170-176 asserts this refusal.
- The mock Palace writes the vertices-only format via write_mfem_mesh (tests:291), so no test exercises the real format.
findings.failure_scenario: The approved run completes Palace level 0 and level 1. execute() then reads post/coupled_chip_cell_L2.mesh (pairing_driver.py:427-428) and raises ValueError. The driver writes failure.json and a manifest, and the one attempt is spent with no level-1 or level-2 static or nesting result.

findings.title: The nesting predicate ('every new vertex is a coarse-edge midpoint') rejects Palace's genuinely nested level-1 to level-2 bisection refinement, so the record is UNQUALIFIED
findings.evidence:
MFEM mechanism:
- GeneralRefinement on a conforming tet mesh calls LocalRefinement(type 3): 7 marked-edge bisections per marked tet, then green closure (mesh.cpp:10509-10560; the 3D branch of LocalRefinement).
- Bisection always splits the element's current first edge. For a TYPE_PF tet, new_redges become (2,4)/(3,1) (mesh.cpp:10814, 10829).
- Cases 3 and 4 then give grandchildren whose next refinement edge contains the child's new vertex.
- MarkEdge never assigns PF at level 0, but closure-bisected level-1 tets can be PF. So the second level adds vertices that are not midpoints of level-1 edges.

Emulated pairing box (count-validated path):
- L1→L2 adds 19,452 new vertices, 209 of them not level-1 edge midpoints: 208 at barycentric (1/2, 1/4, 1/4) and 1 at (3/4, 1/4).
- pd.nesting returns new_vertices_are_coarse_edge_midpoints=False, max_midpoint_offset_rel=1.42e-2, nested=False.

The refinement is nonetheless nested:
- Exhaustive barycentric location puts every level-2 vertex inside a level-1 tet (min barycentric -1.8e-15).
- The Galerkin identity with a general barycentric P holds to 1.49e-14.
- 3,000 sampled fine tets each lie inside one coarse tet (min barycentric -3.9e-14).

The same failure appears on the emulated N1R→N2R box, whose element/vertex/edge/face counts match Palace's logs exactly: 2,780 new vertices, nested=False. L0→L1 passes (3,309/3,309).

Misstated claims:
- The docstring 'bisection and red refinement both add only edge midpoints' (pairing_driver.py:196-197) and report §4 ('every new vertex must be a coarse edge midpoint') are contradicted by MFEM source.
- verify_nesting.py and nesting_verification.json check af.refine_red, a refinement Palace does not perform.
findings.failure_scenario: The run completes all three levels. nesting(level1, level2) returns nested=False. integrity() then adds 'levels 1->2: refinement not verified nested' (pairing_driver.py:324-326), and the verdict is UNQUALIFIED regardless of S, B or H. The single attempt is spent on a false integrity failure.

findings.title: Integrity requires exactly 6 modes, but Palace writes every converged eigenpair (N2R wrote 9 with N=6)
findings.evidence:
- eigensolver.cpp:264 sets num_conv = eigen->Solve().
- eigensolver.cpp:292 loops `for (int i = 0; i < num_conv; i++)` and writes eig.csv and port-EPR.csv rows for every converged mode. Solver.Eigenmode.N is a request, not a cap.
- Committed evidence with "N": 6: N2R eig.csv has 9 rows (log line 276: 'Found 9 converged eigenvalues'); R1 has 7 rows; L2 and N1R have 6.
- integrity() fails any level with n_modes != modes_saved (pairing_driver.py:305-306; predeclaration integrity.modes_saved = 6).
- band() uses all rows (pairing_driver.py:244-256), while the predeclaration defines B over 'the 6 saved modes'.
- Level 1 (about 102k DOFs, emulated) is the same size class as N2R (103k), which returned 9.
findings.failure_scenario: Palace converges 7 to 9 eigenpairs at level 1 or level 2. integrity() adds 'level k: 9 modes saved, not 6', and the verdict is UNQUALIFIED. If the rule were simply relaxed after the fact, B and H would be computed over a different mode set than predeclared.
findings.suggested_fix: Before approval, predeclare the band as the lowest 6 rows by Re f (the rows are written in solver order; state and verify that ordering), and require n_modes >= 6. Record the extra modes descriptively only. Alternatively, predeclare all converged modes as the band and drop the equality rule. Freeze either choice in predeclaration.json and add a test with a 9-row eig.csv.

findings.title: surface-Q.csv, a raw Palace output for this config, is not copied into the evidence record
findings.evidence: PALACE_OUTPUTS (pairing_driver.py:80-81) lists eig, port-EPR, domain-E, palace.json, error-indicators, port-V and port-I. The committed L2 and N2R postpro directories also contain surface-Q.csv, which Palace writes because the base config sets Boundaries.Postprocessing.Dielectric on attribute 10. Only allow-listed files are copied into results/ (pairing_driver.py:420-422).
findings.failure_scenario: The committed record omits a raw solver output. It survives only in the 90-day workflow artefact, contrary to CLAUDE.md §4 (raw solver output first) and the report's 'raw Palace outputs' claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy every file in postpro/ except the refined .mesh, or add surface-Q.csv to the list and fail closed on unexpected missing files.

findings.title: The report says nesting is verified 'before anything is read', but the driver solves and records the static quantity and the band before the nesting check
findings.evidence: pairing_driver.py:433-441 runs static_capacitance on the refined mesh and writes static.json and band.json before nesting() and nesting.json. Report §4 says 'Each step is verified nested before anything is read.' The verdict is still computed only after integrity(), so this is a wording defect.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of the record assumes the static solve was gated on verified nesting when it was not. The verdict path is unaffected.
findings.suggested_fix: Either run nesting() before static_capacitance, or reword the report to say the verdict is gated on nesting.

findings.title: The level-3 DOF estimate (1.3–2.9 M) overstates the emulated count
findings.evidence: The count-validated emulation gives 1,111,691 ND DOFs at box level 3 (87,213 marked tets), against the report's 1.3–2.9 M. Levels 1 and 2 (102,280 and 235,655) fall inside the stated ranges.
findings.failure_scenario: None for this test, since level 3 is excluded. It could mislead a future feasibility decision.
findings.suggested_fix: State the number as an estimate, or replace it with an MFEM-emulated count.

reviews.summary:
Adversarial review (lens: experimental design, evidence governance, honesty of claims). Snapshot: the work under review is no longer uncommitted. It was committed and pushed as 72aec5479ae0 on palace/physical-coupled-candidate, the tree is clean, and I reviewed that commit. I modified nothing under /home/user/QMHP-CEM (git status unchanged, no caches written). Scratch work is in .../scratchpad/redteam/design-lens/. I ran no solve on the QMHP mesh or any refinement of it. The only runs on that mesh were reading it, an MFEM mesh-refinement replica and P1-stiffness assembly. The GitHub calls were read-only list calls.

What I ran:
(a) the driver's own band(), integrity(), decide(), read_mfem_mesh() and nesting() on committed CSVs, synthetic inputs and replica meshes;
(b) a serial replica of Palace's box refinement (geodata.cpp RefineMesh marking + GeneralRefinement(refs,-1), with EnsureNodes as in LoadMesh), built against the pinned MFEM c444b17c. It reproduces Palace's N1R counts exactly (V 14,667 / E 84,485 / T 68,299). It reproduces N2R to within 10 V, 60 E and 50 T (17,457/103,471/84,495 against 17,447/103,411/84,445);
(c) the synthetic sheet-port delta at slab n = 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8;
(d) tests/test_static_band_pairing.py: 35 passed.

The three blocking defects each end the single attempt after at least one Palace solve without a verdict. The synthetic end-to-end tests cannot see any of them, because the mock Palace writes a vertices-only mesh, exactly 6 modes, and uses red refinement.

Checks that HOLD:
- The numbers in the report match identities.json, nesting_verification.json and the committed CSVs: Σ|p|/f² 0.467302; 1/S0 0.466994; δ 6.59e-4; 0.39% margin; H/B 0.9912–0.9962; synthetic +2.3%/+3.0%/-2.7%; Galerkin 6.9e-15; volumes 2.2e-15; 3,040 walls; 543 edges; controls 0.953/0.954/1.055. The only imprecisions are that '0.996 for the 6-mode bands' omits L3 at 0.9952, and the 'a fifth of ×1.39' arithmetic (see findings).
- The box marks exactly 1,880 tets.
- DOF feasibility holds. The replica gives 102,313 DOF at level 1 and 235,595 at level 2: inside the stated ranges and far under the 450k cap.
- The conformity argument for C ≤ C_h and the nesting argument for monotonicity are sound. The 82.2 fF bound is correctly limited to the meshed model.
- SaveAdaptMesh with MGMaxLevels 1 does write <Output>/coupled_chip_cell_L2.mesh: capacity 1 leads RefineMesh to call RebalanceMesh, and the BaseSolver constructor creates postpro before ReadMesh.
- The level-0 re-run is safe. N1 against N1R, the same problem with MGMaxLevels changed, differs in f1 by 4.6e-9, against the 1e-5 tolerance.
- Interface boundary elements Palace adds get new attributes (≥13), so they cannot collide with 2, 4 or 10.
- The cannot_establish lists (E_C, Route A, convergence) are clear.

Caveats:
- My replica is serial MFEM and not bit-identical to Palace's ParMesh at level 2. The non-midpoint phenomenon is structural (212 cases for the pairing box, 64 for the N2R box), not marginal.
- The static-anchor S0 was computed in this sandbox (platform Linux-6.18.44-fc-v37), not on the GitHub runner. The 1e-10 level-0 reproduction tolerance is plausible for a direct solve (residual 4.3e-16) but untested across platforms.
- On the synthetic aligned slab, δ moved from 2.99% (n=4) to 2.04% (n=8): the sheet-port δ is itself mesh-dependent at the ~1-point level per halving on a large port. The real port's δ0 is only 6.6e-4.

Not established by this review: an actual Palace run, which I could not do (no Docker daemon) and which was not allowed. Before approval, the fixes must be predeclared again, with new config digests where configs change.

findings.title: Palace saves the refined mesh with a 'nodes' section, which read_mfem_mesh refuses: the attempt fails at level 1 after the level-1 solve
findings.evidence:
- Where the driver refuses: pairing_driver.py:160-161 raises ValueError('curved mesh (nodes section): refused') when 'vertices N' is followed by 'nodes'. Lines 427-428 read the level-1 and level-2 meshes with that reader.
- Why Palace writes a nodes section: LoadMesh at pinned Palace geodata.cpp:1553-1570 calls mesh->EnsureNodes() unless Model.RemoveCurvature is set. Its default is false (configfile.hpp:209), and the base config and the level configs do not set it.
- Every committed Palace log (L2, N1R, N2R, L3, R1, PO1, N1, N2) prints 'Mesh curvature order: 1' after RefineMesh. That line is printed only when GetNodes() is non-null (geodata.cpp:376).
- The save path: RebalanceMesh (geodata.cpp:1403-1441) saves via mesh->GetSerialMesh(0).
- In pinned MFEM c444b17c, pmesh.cpp:5466-5490 gives the serial mesh an H1 nodal space when Nodes exist and sets every vertex to 0.0. Mesh::Printer (mesh.cpp:11413-11424) then writes 'vertices N' followed by 'nodes / FiniteElementSpace / H1_3D_P1'.
- Reproduced: my MFEM replica wrote exactly this layout ('vertices\n17305\n\nnodes'), and pd.read_mfem_mesh on it raises 'curved mesh (nodes section): refused'.
- The driver's own test (test_static_band_pairing.py:170) asserts this refusal, and the mock Palace writes a vertices-only file (line 291). So the tests encode the wrong assumption.
findings.failure_scenario:
1. Level 0 runs and is recorded.
2. The level-1 Palace eigen solve completes.
3. read_mfem_mesh raises, the except-BaseException path writes failure.json, and the one attempt is spent. Level 2 never runs.

A reader that took coordinates from the vertices section instead would get all-zero coordinates.
findings.suggested_fix:
Parse the nodes section: FiniteElementCollection H1_3D_P1; read VDim and Ordering; take each vertex's coordinates from its vertex vdofs; refuse anything that is not P1. The alternative is to predeclare Model.RemoveCurvature: true as an additional delta (new config digests, and level 0 re-checked against L2).

Either way, make the mock write the exact layout MFEM prints (vertices count, then nodes, with zeroed vertex data) so the test would have caught this.

findings.title: The nesting check is a false negative for MFEM bisection at level 1→2, so a nested refinement is recorded as 'not verified nested' (UNQUALIFIED)
findings.evidence:
- What the check requires: nesting() (lines 207-216) requires every new fine vertex to be the midpoint of a coarse edge, and returns nested=False before any Galerkin test otherwise.
- What Palace actually does: GeneralRefinement(refs,-1), i.e. MFEM LocalRefinement type 3. That is 7 bisections per marked tet plus green closure by repeated bisection. Closure elements left at partial bisection generations after round 1 continue bisecting in round 2, and there they split edges that were created in round 2.
- Replica calibration: the pinned-MFEM replica reproduces Palace's N1R counts exactly and N2R to within 0.06%.
- Pairing box: level 0→1 passes (3,314 new vertices, all midpoints; Galerkin 1.7e-15). At level 1→2, 212 of 19,438 new vertices are not midpoints of level-1 edges (max offset 1.4e-2 × scale). 192 of them bisect a segment from a level-1 vertex to a round-2 vertex.
- N1R/N2R box, for comparison: 64 of 2,790 fail.
- Running the driver's own pd.nesting(level1, level2) on the replica meshes returns {'new_vertices_are_coarse_edge_midpoints': False, 'nested': False}. integrity() then adds 'levels 1->2: refinement not verified nested'.
- The refinement is genuinely nested: a general prolongation (barycentric P1 interpolation of each fine vertex in its level-1 tet) gives a Galerkin identity P^T K2 P - K1 of 8.0e-15 on the same meshes.
- Scope of the earlier checks: verify_nesting.py and the tests validated nesting only against the Python refine_red, never against MFEM's bisection output.
findings.failure_scenario:
1. All three Palace solves and the static solves succeed.
2. The 1→2 nesting step reports nested=False.
3. The record is UNQUALIFIED and the single attempt is spent on a check artefact.
findings.suggested_fix:
Build P by point location: find each fine vertex's containing coarse tet and use its barycentric weights (require min barycentric coordinate ≥ -1e-12). Then test the Galerkin identity and the constraint-set nesting with that P.

Add a regression test on an MFEM-bisection-refined mesh; the replica meshes can be generated offline without Palace.

Predeclare the changed criterion before approval.

findings.title: Integrity requires exactly 6 rows in eig.csv, but Palace returns every converged pair: with the same eigen config N2R returned 9, R1 7 and PO1 8
findings.evidence:
- The rule: integrity() lines 305-306 reject n_modes != modes_saved (predeclaration.json:84, 6). band() uses all rows. Palace eigensolver.cpp:264-292 post-processes every num_conv pair, and num_conv can exceed N.
- The data: the committed runs with Eigenmode N=6, Tol 1e-6, Target 0.5 are L2 (6 rows), N1R (6), N2R (9), R1 (7) and PO1 (8). N2R is the same eigen config, with MGMaxLevels 1 and a 2-level box: 'Found 9 converged eigenvalues'.
- Reproduced: pd.band() on N2R's committed postpro gives n_modes 9. pd.integrity() on a record otherwise all-passing returns ['level 2: 9 modes saved, not 6'].
- No predeclared rule: the predeclaration defines B and H over 'the 6 saved modes' and has no rule for nconv > 6. Using all rows would itself move N2R's H/B from 0.99477 (lowest 6) to 0.99119 (all 9).
findings.failure_scenario:
1. Level 1 or 2, most likely level 2 as in N2R, returns 7 to 9 converged modes.
2. The record is UNQUALIFIED with 'N modes saved, not 6', after all solves have run.
findings.suggested_fix:
Predeclare, before approval, that B, H and δ use the 6 lowest modes by Re f. Require at least 6 converged rows. Record and report extra rows descriptively.

Add a mock case with 9 rows.

findings.title: The synthetic end-to-end tests are said to 'prove both paths', but the mock differs from real Palace in exactly the three ways that spend the attempt
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer approves on the basis that the evidence path is 'proved', and the one attempt then fails on format, mode count or the nesting check.
findings.suggested_fix:
- Reword the report to 'exercises the driver's plumbing under an idealised mock'.
- Rebuild the mock to emit MFEM's real saved-mesh layout, more than 6 converged rows, and MFEM-bisection meshes. The replica meshes can be generated with the pinned MFEM, without Palace.
- Re-run before approval.

findings.title: The workflow is not registered on the default branch, so it cannot be dispatched as the approval procedure describes
findings.evidence:
- Not registered: GitHub list_workflows (read-only) returns 7 workflows and static-band-pairing.yml is not among them. origin/main's .github/workflows has no such file.
- The project already knows the rule. Commit 30fca75's message says: 'GitHub registers a workflow_dispatch workflow from the default branch, so this file must exist on main before it can be dispatched at all.' That is why first-moment-n2r.yml was merged to main in PR #9.
- The procedure omits it: how_to_grant_it (PAIRING-APPROVAL.draft.json:3) and report §6 ('committing ... and dispatching the workflow once') leave out the registration step. That step is itself a merge to main, which CLAUDE.md §3 puts behind human approval.
findings.failure_scenario:
1. The human commits the approval and tries to dispatch.
2. The workflow is not dispatchable.
3. An ad-hoc registration or a workaround is then improvised under time pressure, outside the reviewed procedure.
findings.suggested_fix:
Declare the registration step in the approval procedure: a byte-identical file on main (sha256 pinned), approved separately, with the note that it authorises nothing.

Bind the workflow_ref and ref in the approval, as run_authority.py does for the first-moment workflow.

findings.title: Commit-back pushes without pull --rebase, so any push to the branch during the run loses the evidence commit and leaves the record only in a 90-day artefact
findings.evidence:
- The step: the commit step (lines 151-163) runs git add, git commit, then `git push origin HEAD:$BRANCH`.
- The existing pattern: palace-order1-ladder.yml:232 and palace-coupled-pilot.yml:175 both run `git pull --rebase --autostash origin <ref>` before pushing. The new workflow drops this.
- Exposure: the run spans the image build plus three solves, estimated at 15-30 min or more. The final gate step (165-173) does not check the commit step's outcome.
- Partial records: the commit is gated only on the file-kind check, not on the manifest check. A record left partial by a SIGKILL or job timeout (no failure.json, no manifest) is committed without any marker.
findings.failure_scenario:
1. A human or CI commit lands on palace/physical-coupled-candidate mid-run.
2. The push is rejected as non-fast-forward.
3. The only copy of the record is the uploaded artefact, retained for 90 days. The next checkout has no record directory, so only the run-number binding blocks a re-run.
findings.suggested_fix:
- Add `git pull --rebase --autostash` and a bounded retry before the push.
- On persistent failure, fail loudly and name the artefact.
- When manifest.verify fails or neither summary.json nor failure.json exists, put INCOMPLETE in the commit message and add a marker file.

findings.title: The decisive level-1 and level-2 inputs (the refined meshes) survive only as a 90-day artefact; hashes alone cannot reproduce S1, S2 or the nesting verdict
findings.evidence:
- Where the meshes go: upload-artifact with retention-days: 90 (lines 132-141). Report line 233 says 'never committed; their sha256s are in the record'. mesh.json stores sha256 plus a runner temp path.
- Size: the replica refined meshes are 3.3 MB (level 1) and 7.7 MB (level 2) in MFEM text. That is small enough to commit under a permitted file class or to attach to an immutable release.
- Policy: CLAUDE.md §11 asks for large meshes as 'immutable workflow/release evidence'. §4 requires the raw evidence to survive.
- Consequence: after 90 days the static values at levels 1 and 2, and the nesting result, can be checked only by re-running Palace, which is a new consequential run.
findings.failure_scenario: A later audit or correction (CLAUDE.md §1) needs to re-verify S2 or the Galerkin identity after the artefact has expired. Only digests remain.
findings.suggested_fix:
Commit the two .mesh files (they are about 11 MB in total), or add a declared release-asset upload, with sha256s bound in the manifest.

At minimum, predeclare where the meshes will live permanently.

findings.title: The power condition and most of SUPPORTS are already implied by seen data and by an identity; the report presents them as untested predictions
findings.evidence:
- S tracks H by an identity. By the report's own theorem, S = H(1+δ) on every mesh, with δ = 0 exactly for the lumped port. So 'band and static co-move' is algebra, not a prediction (§3 table, line 153).
- g is effectively determined by committed data. The N1R/N2R box is strictly inside the pairing box (x [-0.62,-0.58] ⊂ [-0.7,-0.5], y [-0.125,-0.065] ⊂ [-0.125,0.1], z [-0.01,0.01] ⊂ [-0.02,0.02]), so the marked set is a superset and the refinement is finer. Committed N2R already has H_N2R/H_L2 = 1.090.
- Reproduced: feeding the committed L2/N1R/N2R bands into pd.decide() as levels 0/1/2 with constant δ = 6.6e-4 gives g = 1.090, drift 0.0049, SUPPORTS. So LOW POWER (g < 1.05) is essentially unreachable.
- H/B is already known: 0.99607 (L2), 0.99620 (N1R), 0.99477 (N2R, lowest 6).
- What is genuinely unknown: only δ_h, the sheet-port perturbation, at the refined levels.
- Report line 201 says 'the windows were fixed before any refined QMHP value existed'. That is true for static values only; refined band values (N1R, N2R) were in hand and inform both g and the drift.
- CLAUDE.md §7: agreement between calculations sharing the same inputs is not independent confirmation.
findings.failure_scenario: The run returns SUPPORTS and it is read as independent evidence that the band or Route A is validated by the static quantity. In fact it shows only that δ stayed below 1% and that H/B did not move.
findings.suggested_fix:
- Reframe the question as measuring δ_h (the sheet port against the lumped element in the −1 moment) and H/B under port-region refinement.
- State in the predeclaration that g ≈ 1.09 is expected from N2R.
- Drop or justify the LOW POWER interpretation 'the static error lies outside the box'.
- In §3 and in the verdict text, say that SUPPORTS is not independent confirmation.

findings.title: The drift is defined on B, the non-robust arithmetic moment, so weak high modes can move the verdict while S and H do not
findings.evidence:
- The rule: decide() lines 276-279 use r_h = S_h/B_h. δ = S/H − 1 already captures co-movement of S with the band. The drift adds only H/B, the band's dispersion, which the report itself calls 'not robust' (line 128).
- Sensitivity, on N2R's lowest 5 modes plus one extra mode at 11 GHz:
  - |p| = 2e-4 moves r by 0.99% while H moves 3.8e-6;
  - |p| = 6e-4 moves r by 2.9%, at the 3% CONTRADICTS threshold.
- Observed so far: high-mode |p| up to 6.2e-5 (N2R mode 8) and 4.2e-5 (L3 mode 6). N2R's lowest-6 band already contributes a 0.13% H/B shift against L2.
- Band membership also changes under refinement: L2's modes 3-6 (5.1-8.7 GHz) are absent in N1R.
findings.failure_scenario: A port-localised or weakly coupled mode with |p| of a few 1e-4 enters the 6-mode band at level 2. SUPPORTS drops to UNRESOLVED (drift > 1%), or to CONTRADICTS near 3%, although S and H co-move exactly.
findings.suggested_fix:
Make the decisive quantities δ_h and H_h/H_0 against S_h/S_0, and report B only descriptively.

Otherwise, predeclare a mode-admission rule and report the H/B change as a separate labelled component.

findings.title: The CONTRADICTS reason string says 'decouple' even when only the sheet-port δ exceeded 3%
findings.evidence:
- The code: decide() lines 285-286 return the single reason 'the band and the static quantity decouple under refinement' for (max|δ| > 0.03 OR drift > 0.03).
- The predeclaration's table (predeclaration.json outcomes) separates the two causes. The δ cause is 'Palace's sheet port departs from the lumped element', a port-model effect, not decoupling.
- Reproduced: levels with δ = 3.5% and drift 2e-5 give verdict CONTRADICTS, reason '...decouple under refinement'.
- Relevance: on the synthetic slab, δ changes by about 1 point per halving (2.99% at n=4, 2.04% at n=8), so the δ route is a live one.
findings.failure_scenario: summary.json, the machine-readable verdict, attributes a sheet-port artefact to static-band decoupling, and downstream readers act on the wrong mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit sub-labels such as CONTRADICTS(delta) and CONTRADICTS(drift), each with its own predeclared text, and add a test for each branch.

findings.title: The one-attempt binding is weaker and more brittle than the project's established run_authority
findings.evidence:
- What is checked: require_approval (line 356) checks only GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER == approval and GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT == '1'. It does not check repository, workflow_ref, workflow path or ref. The first-moment approval binds all of these (EXECUTION-APPROVAL.json one_attempt).
- Brittleness: run number 1 is consumed by any dispatch that dies early: a wrong confirmation string, the approval not yet committed, an image-build failure, or a registration test dispatched against main.
- Precedent: first-moment-n2r run #1 (35721700281) was consumed and the approval had to be superseded to run 2.
- The record-directory guard works only if the previous record was committed; see the push finding.
findings.failure_scenario:
Case 1: a refused or failed dispatch spends run 1, and the committed approval can never be satisfied, so a new approval is needed.

Case 2: any other workflow's run #1 invoking --execute with the approval in its checkout passes the gate.
findings.suggested_fix:
Reuse run_authority.py-style binding (repository, workflow_ref, ref, run_number, attempt).

Document that the approval is committed only immediately before a single dispatch, with a procedure for superseding it if the run is consumed without launching.

findings.title: The time model DOF^1.3 is not derived from the relevant local-refinement data, and the closure-factor range excludes the measured N1R value
findings.evidence:
- Report lines 209-213 and the predeclaration feasibility section scale time as DOF^1.3 from N2R.
- The only local-refinement pair, L2 → N2R (79,944 → 103,411 DOF, 78.5 s → 158.7 s), gives a total-time exponent of 2.7. Its estimator solve went from 31.3 s to 79.7 s.
- The stated '10-17 min' lower end is inconsistent: 227k at ^1.3 gives 7.4 min.
- The closure factor '1.4-2.4 measured on the N1R/N2R box' excludes N1R's measured value: 3,865 / (7 × 221) = 2.50.
- At the replica's level-2 DOF (235,595) the estimate is 7.8 min at ^1.3 and about 25 min at ^2.7. Both are under the 2,700 s cap, so feasibility holds.
findings.failure_scenario: The conclusion does not change, but the estimates presented as its basis are unsupported. If the box changes, the same method could under-predict a timeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the DOF from an offline MFEM refinement replica (it matches N1R exactly), and bracket time with the measured exponents (1.15 uniform, 2.7 local). Correct the closure range.

findings.title: Provenance gaps in the approval binding: no image ID in the record; environment and gate code unbound
findings.evidence:
- Image: code_sha256 binds docker/palace.Dockerfile but not the built image ID. The workflow prints the image ID only to the job log (line 89), and the driver records the tag 'qmhp-cem/palace:0.13.0' in palace_run.json, not the ID. The first-moment approval named a full immutable image ID.
- Environment: uv.lock and pyproject, which fix the scipy/numpy versions behind the static solve and the 1e-10 level-0 reproduction, are not bound.
- Gate code: scripts/check_record_files.py and orchestrator/cem.py, used as gates, are not bound.
- Reference platform: S0 was computed in this sandbox (static-anchor summary platform Linux-6.18.44-fc-v37), not on the runner.
findings.failure_scenario: The job log expires, or a lockfile change alters the static solve between approval and dispatch. The record then cannot show which image or numerical stack produced it (CLAUDE.md §5).
findings.suggested_fix: Write the image ID and the PALACE_COMMIT check into the record from the driver, and bind uv.lock and the gate scripts in code_sha256.

findings.title: A manifest failure on the success path produces a contradictory record
findings.evidence: If _finish (line 458) raises after summary.json has been written, the except-BaseException block (459-465) writes failure.json with 'FAILED - the one attempt is spent', then re-manifests. The record then holds both a verdict and a FAILED marker.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient I/O problem during manifest verification leaves summary.json with, for example, SUPPORTS next to failure.json FAILED. Readers can pick either.
findings.suggested_fix: Track the phase. After summary.json is written, a manifest failure should write a distinct manifest_failure.json that references the existing summary instead of declaring the run FAILED.

findings.title: Small overstatements and arithmetic slips in the report and predeclaration
findings.evidence:
- Line 64-65 says 'the two independent energy evaluations in the record agreed exactly'. The P1 energy and the edge energy of the discrete gradient are algebraically identical, so they are not independent (CLAUDE.md §7).
- Line 197 and predeclaration.json:112 say '5% is a fifth of the ×1.39'. A fifth of 0.39 is 7.8%.
- '0.996 for the 6-mode bands' omits L3 at 0.9952.
- predeclaration.json:79 lists 'e²/(2C_2) as a lower bound on E_C,F1F1 under A-R' and a three-point extrapolation as descriptive outputs. The driver computes neither, and the first sits uneasily with 'E_C UNAVAILABLE' and the approval's 'reporting any value as E_C'.
findings.failure_scenario: Minor misreadings of the strength of the evidence, or an E_C-adjacent number appearing in a later write-up.
findings.suggested_fix:
- Call the energy check an 'algebraic consistency check'.
- Fix the threshold rationale.
- Remove the E_C lower bound and the extrapolation from the descriptive list, or implement them with explicit 'not E_C' labelling.
